title: gtm-template-pixel: template.tpl
supports: Opened with WebFetch (TikTok's own Google Tag Manager web template; repository updated 8 September 2026). Maps GA4 events to Pixel events (purchase to CompletePayment, sign_up to CompleteRegistration, begin_checkout to InitiateCheckout, view_item to ViewContent); passes an event_id for deduplication with the Events API; ttq.identify for advanced matching, with the Pixel hashing plain email and phone; needs the TikTok base code; no consent logic visible in the template.

title: gtm-template-eapi: template.tpl
supports: Opened with WebFetch (TikTok's own server-side Google Tag Manager template; repository updated 30 May 2024). Sends to the Events API v1.3 endpoint with an access token header; event_id for deduplication; reads ttclid from the URL and stores it in a first-party cookie for 30 days; reads the _ttp cookie; lowercases, trims and SHA-256 hashes email and phone; hashes external_id; test_event_code; server containers only.

title: The Digital Services Act
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Last update 1 October 2026. Complete ban on targeted ads to children; no ad targeting on sensitive data; ads labelled with who placed them and why; very large platforms keep public ad repositories; deceptive design banned.

title: Article 50: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems
publisher: European Commission AI Act Service Desk
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Text as at 27 July 2026. Providers mark synthetic audio, images and video in a machine-readable way; deployers disclose deepfakes, with lighter duties for clearly artistic or satirical work; information given clearly at first exposure.

publisher: European Commission AI Act Service Desk
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Undated page reflecting the Digital Omnibus. Article 50 transparency rules apply from 2 August 2026; providers of synthetic-content systems placed on the market before then have until 2 December 2026 for Article 50(2).

title: Disclosures 101 for Social Media Influencers
supports: Opened with WebFetch. November 2019. Disclose any material connection; put the disclosure in the video, spoken and on screen; plain words such as "ad" or "sponsored"; a platform disclosure tool alone may not be enough.

title: Influencers' guide to making clear that ads are ads
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Fourth edition dated 23 October 2026, made with the CMA; covers when influencer content must be disclosed as advertising and how to label it, updated for the Digital Markets, Competition and Consumers Act. Page text summarised; full guidance is a PDF.

title: Guidelines 2/2023 on Technical Scope of Art. 5(3) of ePrivacy Directive, Version 2.0
supports: Opened with WebFetch (PDF saved and text extracted). Adopted 7 October 2024. Tracking pixels and tracking links fall under Art. 5(3) (paras 47 to 51); hashed identifiers collected by client-side code are covered (paras 61 to 63); applicability does not always mean consent is needed (para 56).

title: Report of the work undertaken by the Cookie Banner Taskforce
supports: Opened with WebFetch (PDF saved and text extracted). Adopted 17 January 2023. No consent-requiring cookies before a positive action (para 7); no reject option is an infringement for most authorities (para 8); pre-ticked boxes invalid (para 10); legitimate interest cannot justify placing cookies (para 24).

title: Data (Use and Access) Act factsheet: PEC Regulations
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Published 27 June 2025. Revised PECR regulation 6 keeps the ban on storing or accessing information on a device unless an exception applies; new exception for statistics on how an online service is used; changes commence in stages. Used because ico.org.uk returns HTTP 403 to automated fetches.
